exposure: local anesthetic administration into the epidural space following spinal anesthesia
cohort: The study included 404 singleton parturients who underwent elective cesarean sections with spinal anesthesia after 37 weeks of gestation.
finding: Higher BMI, previous cesarean sections, placenta previa/low-lying placenta, and local anesthetic administration into the epidural space after spinal anesthesia significantly prolonged the spinal anesthesia-to-delivery interval, which was in turn inversely correlated with umbilical arterial pH.
